title: MCP tool design
subtitle: Tools shaped as jobs, cost stated on every call, every write read back, every create with a delete: the written standard every MCP tool in my estate must meet.

stats.label: tokens of tool schema an agent had carried every turn
meeting tools, each with a minimal exact schema

lede: FAFOHive: when I added in-house social integrations to the tool hub, the fast path was to generate one tool per vendor endpoint. I took it once. The X module's first build compiled its tools straight from the vendor's OpenAPI specification. They were cheap to make, expensive to call and easy for an agent to misuse. I withdrew that surface and replaced it with tools shaped like the jobs agents actually do, trading generated breadth for designed workflow tools with costs and guards. I wrote the standard every tool in the estate has to meet, and its rulings. Its first rule is that a tool is a job.
quote: An agent cannot budget what it cannot see, so every call states its cost.
evidence: MCP server design: a written standard for every tool, shaped as a job, with a stated cost formula, verbatim errors, read-back writes and a delete for every create.
Tool surface design for agents: ~42,000 tokens of per-turn tool schema replaced by one discovery tool whose 520-character description is held by a test.
Lifecycle testing of agent tools: every kind of post and media created, checked and deleted through agent tools alone, finding 3 platform-semantics defects.
Agent-safe API integration: 24 meeting tools with minimal exact schemas and typed refusals where Microsoft offers no supported action.
author: Corey James
